name: NY-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: Tonko holds a roughly twenty-to-one fundraising advantage over Ambrosio
District leans Democratic by about eight points plus a standard incumbency edge
Prediction markets price Democratic retention near 97 percent
No polls or expert ratings flag any competitive risk
model.rationale: Tonko combines a Democratic-leaning district with an overwhelming financial edge, and prediction markets price his re-election near certainty; no polling or expert ratings point to a competitive race.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or a sharp national shift toward the GOP could narrow what is otherwise a comfortable margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Democratic incumbent Paul Tonko seeks re-election in a district that leans about eight points Democratic, facing Republican Ralph Ambrosio, a challenger with minimal financial backing. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, candidate resources, and market pricing.

Tonko has raised roughly $1.2 million and holds about $467,000 on hand, while Ambrosio has raised about $61,000 with little cash remaining and no reported outside support. Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 97 percent chance of holding the seat. The combination of incumbency, a favorable district lean, and a large resource gap points to a comfortable Tonko win, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact margin.
